title: skipped-sessions.json write is non-atomic and a corrupt/partial file is silently reset then overwritten, losing accumulated rows; concurrent ticks race (read-modify-write)
evidence: recordSkipped uses plain writeFileSync (no temp+rename). readSkippedRecords returns {} on JSON.parse failure, so the next write replaces a truncated file with only the current tick's rows. Probe: truncated a 4-row file to 60 bytes, ran a real tick -> 0 rows remain. Two overlapping ticks both read then write, last writer wins. Same pattern as schedule-state.json precedent. Rows for currently-skipped sessions are re-derived each tick, so loss is limited to history of sessions no longer in the poll window.
fix_direction: Write to temp + fsync + rename (as schedule-state.ts does for the other file); on parse failure rename the bad file aside instead of overwriting. Not security class; file-don't-fix is acceptable at the Approver's discretion.

title: mutation survivor: recordedAt preservation across ticks is unasserted; and mode 0600 is only set at file creation and has no effect on Windows
evidence: Replacing `entries[k]?.recordedAt ?? nowIso` with `nowIso` passes all 6 tests, so a start-less row re-skipped every tick never ages out. writeFileSync mode only applies on create and Windows ignores POSIX modes; the manifest/doc mention 0600 without that caveat. No secret is persisted (key, start, source, tenant only).
fix_direction: Add a test: a no-start row recorded at T0 and re-recorded at T0+31d is dropped. Note in the doc comment that 0600 is POSIX-only.
